target_customer: Row crop farmers in the US growing corn, soybeans and similar crops
problem: Farmers kept field records and equipment data on paper or in disconnected tools and lacked timely, unbiased data to improve yield and profit per acre.
business_model: Freemium farm management SaaS (free at first, premium features added after 2014)
product_category: Agriculture software and field data analytics

founders.name: Jesse Vollmar
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Jan 2017) says he grew up in a farming community and worked in his family's organic corn farm business; after the 2021 sale he became VP of Farm Strategy at Bushel per Feedstuffs.

founders.name: Brad Koch
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: co-founder of FarmLogs, later leading Bushel's Farm team. Concentrate Media says he grew up in rural Michigan's thumb region.

exit.reason: Bushel combined FarmLogs farm level data with its grain and supply chain platform; FarmLogs kept its brand.

competitors.name: The Climate Corporation
competitors.what: Free weather data software plus paid insurance for farm risk; seen by the FarmLogs CEO as the main competitor

competitors.name: Solum (later Granular)
competitors.what: Soil science startup that spun off farm software as Granular, formed 2009
competitors.traction_then: Testing with seven Midwest farmers before launch
competitors.funding_then: Granular raised a 4.2 million Series A later

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting equipment data via cheap Bluetooth hardware and later satellite imagery with predictive models took real data engineering, but the core was an app on standard cloud stacks.

defensibility.rationale: Years of field records and integrations with John Deere, Case and other equipment data created lock in, but Climate Corp had far deeper pockets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Monsanto bought Climate Corp for a reported 930 million dollars (closed Nov 2013) and launched FieldView; FarmLogs stayed independent until Bushel bought it in Jun 2021.

market_need_then: Farmers lacked easy data tools; the founders went to talk to farmers and the CEO said farmers were being ignored by Silicon Valley; more than 50,000 farms used the free product by 2014 per a search summary (not independently opened).

branding.domain_note: Used farmlogs.com, the exact .com; it now redirects to bushelfarm.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Farmer first, plainspoken; CEO publicly said the company would never sell to agribusiness in 2017 per AgFunder headline

rebrands.why: After the acquisition FarmLogs was said to continue under its own brand; the site later redirected to bushelfarm.com, reason not sourced

branding.community_and_virality: Forbes 30 Under 30 recognition for the CEO and regional press in Michigan; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in US row crop agtech with regional and trade press, but no iconic brand assets and the name later folded into Bushel.

outcome_analysis: FarmLogs reached the largest user base among independent farm software startups, raising about 37 million dollars across a seed, Series A in Jan 2014, Series B in Dec 2014 and a 22 million Series C in Jan 2017 led by Naspers. It stayed independent against Monsanto owned Climate Corp until Bushel acquired it in Jun 2021 with terms undisclosed; the buyer was a grain software company, not a pure rescue, though a price was never reported so the investor return is unknown.
notes: Series A exact date not given: Concentrate Media article of 2014-01-29 calls it recent. Seed year 2013 is from the same article ('prior year'); seed investors not named. Series C confirmed by TechCrunch and Naspers release coverage; Prosus in aggregator listings is a later corporate name. A search summary said founders attended Saginaw Valley State University but I could not confirm it in an opened source, so education is left empty. Founding year conflicts (2011 vs 2012). Competitor dates: sources are dated 2014, the closest found; Climate Corp and Granular existed around the 2012 batch. Aggregators put total raised near 37.85M, consistent with the rounds here.
